overview: This Senate resolution marks the 250th anniversary of a March 16, 1776, resolution by the Second Continental Congress, the body that led the American colonies during the Revolution. That 1776 resolution, passed as war with Britain loomed, asked the colonies to observe May 17, 1776, as a day of humiliation, fasting, and prayer, and the Senate resolution quotes its religious language at length. The Senate simply commemorates the anniversary; the resolution creates no observance and changes no law. It was approved on March 18, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution recognizes a historic moment in the founding era and the role faith played for many colonists during the Revolution.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and some may question the Senate highlighting a specifically religious observance.
